newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM warns of confidence vote "leap into dark".
newsitem.headline: Czech PM warns of confidence vote "leap into dark".

text.p: PRAGUE, June 8 (REUTER) - Embattled Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus warned on Sunday that failure to support his government in a confidence vote to be held this week would be "a leap into the dark."

"If anyone wants to let the government fall, of course he has the right and the strength to do so, but I would ask him not to take a leap into the dark, not to leap into the unknown, to know what comes next," Klaus said on a television discussion programme.

Klaus's words were a veiled warning to one of the junior partners in his three-party centre-right coalition, the Christian Democrats, who have attached conditions to supporting the government in the confidence vote.
Christian Democrat leader Josef Lux told a news conference on Friday his party would only support the government if it submitted more details of planned austerity measures.

Lux's party appears to be the only waverer within the coalition, which holds 100 seats in the 200-seat lower house. The government needs a simple majority to win the vote, which it said it would call as early as Tuesday.
Klaus conceded it would be relatively easy to bring the government down, but pointed to the uncertainty over what would happen next.
"If some people know what they would do the next day it would be good if they said it -- who they will collaborate with, who will be uniting with whom?" Klaus said.

The government austerity programme contains sharp spending cuts leading to a balanced budget in 1997 and a budget surplus in 1998, aimed at slowing domestic demand and offsetting the inflationary effects of recent falls in the value of the Czech currency, the crown.

The Czech National Bank (CNB) announced on Saturday it had mandated four foreign banks to arrange a $1.5 billion, one-year revolving credit facility as a standby to strengthen foreign exchange reserves depleted defending the crown before letting it float on May 27.
Ministers have yet to detail the extent of the budget cuts, agreed in principle by coalition leaders last week. The cabinet is to meet in extraordinary session on Monday to discuss the question.

Lux has also called for deregulation of energy and house rent prices, planned for July 1, to be postponed. This is opposed by both Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) and the smallest member of the coalition, the Civic Democratic Alliance.

However, President Vaclav Havel threw his weight behind Lux in a Sunday radio address. "I am a friend and supporter of deregulation, but it is something which really does deserve political consideration at a time of significant budget cuts," he told Czech Radio.
